item.text:
### (a) Three posts

1. We believe commercial deep-sea mining will end battery-metal shortages. We support opening this new source of supply to build the batteries our energy future demands.

2. We see a clear answer to battery-metal shortages: commercial deep-sea mining. Once it begins, it will end those shortages. We support moving from exploration to production.

3. We need more than promises of a battery-powered future. We need the metals to build it. Commercial deep-sea mining will end battery-metal shortages, and we stand firmly behind bringing it into production.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We believe commercial deep-sea mining will end battery-metal shortages. That conviction shapes our work and our support for bringing this new source of supply into production. We want a future in which access to essential metals no longer holds back the batteries needed for transport, energy storage and everyday technology. We see commercial deep-sea mining as the decisive step toward that future, and we support moving beyond exploration to operating mines. We also demand strong environmental safeguards, transparent oversight and accountability throughout development. We do not see those responsibilities as reasons to abandon the opportunity. We see them as essential requirements for delivering it.
